Definition: A group of model applications sharing broad objectives and ways of using SDM outputs to inform conservation decisions. Error severity is assigned at this level in the framework.
Examples: Anthropogenic-disturbance screening belongs to the category “Threshold for restriction or precautionary management.”

Definition: A model criterion assigned error certainty rankings and directly filtered by the framework for the selected model type.
Examples: Perfect detection is a core criterion retained for underprediction in the prediction-model case study.

Definition: Failure to meet a condition represented by a model criterion.
Examples: Species records cover only a narrow portion of the environmental conditions across which the model is applied.

Definition: A value or rule used to translate model outputs, or quantities derived from them, into a category or action.
Examples: Locations exceeding a specified predicted-occurrence value are flagged for precautionary review.

Definition: The ranked likelihood that violation of a criterion will produce a particular error type for a given model type. Rankings are always, sometimes, or rarely (Table 3).
Examples: In the case study, violation of the perfect detection criterion is ranked as always leading to underprediction for prediction models.

Definition: A user-defined selection specifying the minimum error certainty considered when identifying relevant core criteria.
Examples: Selecting sometimes retains criteria whose violation is ranked as sometimes or always producing a relevant error type.

Definition: The ranked consequence of a particular error type for conservation outcomes within an application category. Rankings are correctness, quality, or efficiency (Table 3).
Examples: Underprediction in disturbance screening can leave important locations unprotected and is assigned a correctness consequence.

Definition: A user-defined selection specifying the minimum error severity considered when identifying relevant error types for an application.
Examples: Selecting quality includes error types assigned quality or correctness consequences, but excludes those assigned only efficiency consequences.

Definition: The direction of model error considered in the framework: underprediction or overprediction.
Examples: Underprediction; overprediction.

Definition: The purpose for which SDM outputs are used to inform ecological understanding or conservation decisions.
Examples: Selecting restoration sites; directing invasive-species surveys; screening proposed developments for potential impacts on species.
References: Guisan et al. (2013); Srivastava et al. (2019); Meller et al. (2014)

Definition: Judgement of whether a model is suitable for its intended application, informed by evaluation of its performance, assumptions, and limitations.
Examples: Judging whether a regional SDM is suitable for screening potential development impacts on a species.
References: Araújo et al. (2019); Soley-Guardia et al. (2024)

Definition: An assumption or requirement used to evaluate an SDM, including conditions intended to avoid issues or hazards that can affect its predictions.
Examples: Species data cover the environmental extent; predictor resolution matches the response scale.
References: Araújo et al. (2019); Soley-Guardia et al. (2024)

Definition: The iterative process of assembling and preparing data, building, evaluating, and refining a model, and generating predictions.
Examples: Compiling occurrence records, preparing environmental predictors, fitting and evaluating a model, and generating a prediction map.

Definition: Examination of model performance and plausibility using quantitative measures, qualitative evidence, or both.
Examples: Calculating performance measures using independent data and checking predicted distributions for ecological plausibility.

Definition: The distinction between prediction and projection used in the framework to account for differences in the consequences of criterion violation.
Examples: Prediction; projection.

Definition: A person who uses SDM outputs to inform an ecological or conservation application, whether or not they developed the model.
Examples: A conservation planner using predicted distributions to identify candidate protected areas.

Definition: A person who develops an SDM, including choices about data, model fitting, evaluation, and prediction.
Examples: An ecologist developing an SDM from bird surveys and environmental predictors.

Definition: Prediction of a quantity above its true value, or inclusion of locations that should not be included in a predicted distribution. For binary occurrence predictions, overprediction takes the form of false positives, also termed commission errors.
Examples: A model predicts a density of eight individuals per hectare where the true density is four.
References: Mendes et al. (2020), Velazco et al. (2020)

Definition: Use of fitted species–environment relationships to estimate a species’ distribution or associated quantities within the geographical region and time period represented by the model’s calibration data.
Examples: Mapping current bird density across the region represented by the calibration surveys.

Definition: Transfer of fitted species–environment relationships to estimate a species’ distribution or associated quantities in another geographical region or time period.
Examples: Applying a model calibrated on current conditions to estimate suitable habitat under a future climate scenario.

Definition: A criterion represented as a special case of one or more core criteria, directly or through another related criterion. It is included through these relationships rather than independently assigned error certainty rankings.
Examples: A special case associated with two retained core criteria is displayed beneath each of them without being independently filtered.

Definition: A model relating species occurrence or abundance to environmental variables to estimate distribution, habitat suitability, or density.
Examples: A model relating bird occurrence to forest cover and climate to map predicted occurrence.

Definition: Prediction of a quantity below its true value, or omission of locations that should be included in a predicted distribution. For binary occurrence predictions, underprediction takes the form of false negatives, also termed omission errors.
Examples: A model predicts absence at a site where the species is present.

Definition: The particular use of an SDM described by its application, model type, and user-defined error severity and certainty tolerances.
Examples: Disturbance screening using a prediction model, with correctness selected for severity tolerance and sometimes selected for certainty tolerance.
